trust_decision.summary: The parser decides whether a start tag is a (custom) raw-text/Data element by trimmed+lower-cased name lookup in the TagSet, while the tokeniser decides where that raw text ends using the untrimmed source name; a tag name with a trailing control char is resolved to a safelisted Data tag whose content then swallows markup that the Cleaner copies verbatim as a DataNode.

landing_point.why: Summary names the Cleaner and raw-text elements; this is where DataNode content of a safelisted tag is copied unescaped.

fix_sites.entry_point: Jsoup.clean / Cleaner.clean / Cleaner.isValid / Jsoup.parse and Parser.xmlParser().parseInput (via TreeBuilder.tagFor -> TagSet.valueOf)
fix_sites.module_kind: parser tag registry (lower-level public class TagSet, package-private overload)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: TagSet.valueOf trimming is documented public-API normalisation ('Provide a null normalName unless we already have one; will be normalized'), and the old test trimNormalizeElementNamesInBuilder asserts trimming as intended, so a solver can argue the trim is required behaviour and only patch Token or the Cleaner.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Public TagSet.valueOf/Tag APIs must still trim user-supplied names (e.g. ' p '), custom Data/RcData tags (<x-data>, <custom-rcdata>) must keep raw-text parsing case-insensitively, and the Cleaner must keep copying DataNodes of safelisted data tags; escaping/dropping all DataNodes in the Cleaner or rejecting all non-trimmed names would break these.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Patch only one side (stop trimming in Token.normalName, or in TagSet.valueOf) or escape/strip DataNodes in Cleaner; fixing one side alone leaves the other trimmed lookup resolving 'x-raw\u001E' to the Data tag (TagSet.java:140-148).
